summary: Through the Ages is a dense civilization-building card game where players draft technologies, leaders, and wonders across three ages while balancing culture, production, and military strength. It's widely regarded as one of the deepest civ games on cardboard, with tense decisions about when to invest in military to threaten or deter opponents.
praised: exceptional strategic depth and long-term planning
elegant tension between military, culture, and economy
criticised: brutal learning curve, especially around military mechanics
long playtime that can drag with new players
can feel punishing if you fall behind militarily early

interaction.kind: direct card drafting against each other plus military aggression and action-denial
interaction.detail: Cards are drafted via a shared, dwindling market where taking one directly denies it to opponents, and military strength lets you pillage resources, force civil wars, or tie up an opponent's actions, so a good move is frequently chosen specifically to hurt someone else. Very little of the state is purely internal — even peaceful strategies must constantly react to what rivals are building toward.
interaction.said: widely called "cutthroat", "brutal", "take-that", with reviewers warning the military and civil-action war can wreck an opponent's civilization outright

scoring.how_you_win: You steadily convert culture, technologies, buildings, wonders, and leaders into VP across three ages while defending against military aggression; the game ends when the Age III deck runs out and the highest VP total wins.

_name: Through the Ages: A New Story of Civilization
